public_messages: [Oscar Wali]: The cybersecurity firm's identification of seven vulnerabilities—two of which are high-severity and potentially allow remote access to tabulation servers—raises serious concerns about the integrity of our election infrastructure. While the vendor characterizes these as theoretical, they have failed to demonstrate that these vulnerabilities are not exploitable in real-world conditions. Given the critical role of this software in all 47 counties and the potential for remote compromise, we cannot accept reassurances without verifiable evidence of mitigation. High-severity flaws in election systems demand immediate remediation, not voluntary timelines, to uphold public trust and meet established security standards. We recommend Option 1: requiring full security remediation prior to the next election.
